Across the next hours the lineup tracks battery chemistry changes that could raise output for cars and grid storage at once, new limits on usable water ice near the lunar poles, and two specific hazards OpenAI's chief says must be addressed before larger training runs proceed. Further segments examine shifts in sarcopenia drug research, simultaneous policy meetings at the Bank of Japan and the Federal Reserve, rail network effects on smaller airports, vitamin pricing gaps, teen use of chatbots for late-night support, wetland rules in Alberta, Class40 entries in an upcoming transatlantic race, and a lab catalyst that holds charge far longer than earlier versions. Each program keeps its own feed.

## Mira's field note

At the Paul Scherrer Institute and ETH Zurich, physicists have measured the optical Magnus effect for the first time by directing a tightly focused laser at a single trapped calcium ion. The point of strongest interaction sits a few hundred nanometers off the beam’s apparent center, a sideways shift that depends only on wavelength. The result appears in Physical Review Letters. Future runs will check how the displacement changes when the same beams address qubits.
